articleTitle: Prediction of Axial Load Capacity of Reinforced Concrete Column Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The axial load capacity (ALC) of a reinforced concrete (RC) column is a fundamental aspect of a structure. Thus, the systematic computation process plays a vital role in building design. It is widely encouraged to use artificial neural network (ANN) for this uncommon problem to predict the precise outcome. This study used three different algorithms of the ANN model to forecast the ALC of an RC column provided by its specific properties. These are Bayesian regularization backpropagation (BRB), Levenberg-Marquardt, and scaled conjugate gradient. The given dataset from the literature was trained in MATLAB software, and it was found that the BRB algorithm has a more positive performance compared to other algorithms. This study presents a detailed methodology and results of the model. Utilizing ANN would provide a more accurate and robust tool for predicting and giving new recommendations for professionals to design safer, more economical, and more efficient structures.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Correlation between MQ Gas Sensors with Temperature and Humidity Sensor on an Outdoor Setting
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This study focuses on evaluating the correlation between gas sensors and temperature and humidity, which are environmental factors that can affect the performance of gas sensors. A device was developed integrating the MQ sensors namely MQ2, MQ3, MQ4, MQ5, MQ6, MQ7, MQ8, MQ9, MQ135, and MQ 137 that have integrated temperature and humidity sensors, during both dry and wet seasons. Reading from the device will be collected for the analysis of the correlations. The researchers analyzed the collected data using MATLAB software to determine the correlation between the sensors and to identify which algorithms provided the most accurate results. The result shows that sensors including MQ2, MQ5, MQ6, MQ7, and MQ8, have a high negative correlation with temperature. In contrast, other sensors show only a weak positive correlation, such as MQ3 and MQ9. Notably, MQ135 has a strong positive correlation with temperature, whereas MQ137 shows a significant negative correlation. On the other hand the correlation of the gas sensors shows a weak negative correlation with the humidity.

articleTitle: Predicting the Youth Unemployment Rate in Iraq Until 2035 Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Youth unemployment significantly impacts the socio-economic stability and growth of developing countries, particularly Iraq. This study aims to predict the youth unemployment rate in Iraq until 2035 using advanced AI techniques such as autoregressive integrated moving averages (ARIMA) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). We developed and tested both ARIMA and RNN models using data from 2000 to 2023. The ARIMA (1, 1, 0) model showed strong predictive ability with an R-squared value of 0.954, an RMSE of 1.350, and a MAPE of 3.113. In contrast, the RNN model, enhanced by Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, exhibited superior performance with an RMSE of 0.113, a MAPE of 0.4888, and an R-value of 0.9998. Predictions reveal a rising trend in youth unemployment, expected to increase from 33.22% in 2024 to 45.63% by 2035. These findings underscore the effectiveness of AI-driven models in providing reliable forecasts, which are crucial for policymakers to devise targeted interventions. Additionally, accurate forecasting aligns with several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and supports efforts in poverty reduction and educational alignment with labor market needs. Future research will integrate more socio-economic variables and explore further model enhancements to improve predictive accuracy. This study is valuable for its practical application in socio-economic planning and forecasting to mitigate youth unemployment in Iraq.

articleTitle: Online Partial Discharge Monitoring In Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) and Air Insulated Switchgear (AIS)
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This paper investigates the condition of high voltage gas insulated switchgear (GIS) through an online partial discharge (PD) inspection using ultrasound, Transient Earth Voltage (TEV), and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) techniques. The primary goal was to establish a baseline for effective condition monitoring. The problem addressed is the potential for undetected PD activity to lead to insulation failure, resulting in costly downtime and safety risks. The methodology involved deploying these complementary techniques to capture PD signals from the GIS and AIS operating under normal conditions. The inspection results indicated no significant PD activity, demonstrating the switchgear is in good condition and providing a reliable baseline for future monitoring. The study concludes that periodic PD monitoring is essential for early detection of insulation issues, recommending a 12-month interval for follow-up inspections. This approach enhances the proactive maintenance strategy, ensuring operational safety and reducing the risk of unexpected failures.

articleTitle: Kinematic Modeling and Prototype Development of a Six Degrees-of-Freedom Stewart Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This paper presents kinematic modeling, control system design, and hardware-software systems development of a Stewart platform prototype. The modeling part of the platform includes both forward and inverse kinematics analyses which were then used to design a controller that can regulate the platform’s movement between some desired initial and final positions. Hardware components of the platform were constructed and then integrated with software suites that are developed in NI LabVIEW software for real-time experimental use. Simulation and experimental results are reported to illustrate the performance of the developed platform prototype.

articleTitle: Investigation of Trench No-Core Fiber Sensor for High Refractive Index Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The trench no-core fiber (TNCF) sensor is known for its effectiveness in refractive index (RI) sensing due to its coreless design. Traditionally, TNCF sensors have been limited to measuring RI values below the fiber material’s RI. This study presents a simulation of a TNCF with a trench depth of 30 μm and width of 50 μm, designed for high refractive index (HRI) sensing using COMSOL Multiphysics software. The focus is on leaky mode behavior in HRI analyte mediums, compared to guided mode in low refractive index (LRI) mediums. Performance was evaluated by simulating HRI analyte mediums with RI values from 1.4600 RIU to 1.5500 RIU, observing electric field attenuation due to leaky mode behavior. Results show that the TNCF sensor provides superior sensitivity for detecting HRI mediums, attributed to increased leakage loss of leaky modes relative to trenchless NCF, due to lower mode confinement in TNCF. The sensor achieved a sensitivity of 4149.4 V/mRIU and demonstrated strong linearity with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.8654. Despite these advantages, the TNCF sensor has notable limitations. Sensitivity decreases at extreme refractive index values, and issues with mode confinement led to light leakage, affecting performance consistency. Additionally, the trench design introduces fabrication complexity and increased costs. These limitations suggest that while the TNCF sensor shows significant promise for HRI sensing applications, further optimization and improvements are needed to address these challenges and expand its practical use, including monitoring oil degradation and other HRI environments.

articleTitle: Characterizing Diurnal Heart Rate Variability Patterns with Continuous Wearable Monitoring and Polynomial Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV), a well-established marker of cardiovascular health and autonomic nervous system function, exhibits dynamic fluctuations throughout the day. This study aimed to characterize these diurnal HRV patterns with high precision and detail, utilizing 30 days of continuous heart rate monitoring (Polar H10) in a cohort of 35 healthy adults. The cumulative sum of population standard deviations (SDNN) was employed as the HRV metric, capturing both short-term and long-term variations.A cubic polynomial model was used to characterize the relationship between HRV and time of day, revealing a statistically significant and non-linear pattern. HRV peaked during sleep and early morning hours, gradually declining throughout the day and reaching its lowest point in the evening. This pattern was consistent across participants, yet significant inter-individual variability was observed in the specific shape and magnitude of the diurnal curves. The model demonstrated excellent fit to the data (R-squared = 0.98) and good predictive validity on a separate dataset (Mean of Absolute Error = 58.5 ms).These findings underscore the complex interplay of circadian rhythms, sleep-wake cycles, and behavioral factors in shaping diurnal HRV patterns. The cubic polynomial model effectively captured the non-linearity and individual variability in these patterns, highlighting the importance of using statistical models for characterizing this nuanced physiological measure. The observed inter-individual variability emphasizes the need for personalized health monitoring and intervention strategies that consider an individual’s unique HRV profile for optimizing cardiovascular health and overall well-being.

articleTitle: A Tutorial to Implement a BLDC Motor Speed Control for an Electric Boat Using Simscape and Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The marine sector is moving towards all-electric ships to improve energy efficiency and reduce air pollution. A key part of an electric propulsion system for an electric ship is the electric motor, especially permanent magnet motors, known for their high torque and efficiency. Recently, brushless DC (BLDC) permanent magnet motors have rapidly advanced, matching the pace of electric boat development. These motors are preferred for their efficiency, reliability, and low maintenance, making them suitable for varying water conditions. Despite much research on BLDC motor modeling, there are few tutorial-style guides. This paper offers a step-by-step tutorial for using Simscape and Simulink to control BLDC motors in electric boats. The simulation results demonstrate excellent speed tracking, closely matching the desired speed without overshooting. The system swiftly adjusts to rapid speed changes during acceleration and deceleration, which is essential for applications requiring quick adjustments. This guide helps engineers and researchers design, test, and optimize motor control systems, promoting efficient and sustainable electric boating solutions.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Of Rabin-p And RSA-OAEP Encryption Scheme In Securing Data On Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This paper analyses the Rabin-p encryption scheme on the cloud in terms of runtime on VMware and Amazon Web Services. Amazon provides a comprehensive cloud computing platform called Amazon Web Services (AWS). It provides diverse cloud services, including computing power, storage options, and databases. Therefore, Rabin-p is introduced to Amazon Web Services. The encryption and decryption runtimes and the runtime when uploading ciphertext to AWS have been analyzed. Rabin-p is an asymmetric method that provides increased security. This can help to improve cloud security for both AWS and its clients. The length of primes significantly impacts the speed of encryption and decryption processes, generally resulting in longer processing times for longer primes. In comparative tests across various prime lengths, Rabin-p demonstrated faster encryption and decryption speeds when compared to RSA-OAEP. Specifically, Rabin-p consistently exhibited lower encryption times than RSA-OAEP at prime lengths of 341, 682, and 1365 bits at almost 50% faster but Rabin-p runtime increased while upload and download to the cloud. This suggests that Rabin-p may offer greater efficiency for data at rest.

articleTitle: Real-Time Data Forecasting On Missing Energy Data Using Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Energy data analysis is becoming more important for producing efficient and cost-effective energy by monitoring usage and identifying when energy loses quality. Time series analysis helps predict future trends and supports decision-making. This study uses the SARIMA model to forecast missing energy data from Hospital Rehabilitasi Cheras. The model’s performance was measured using Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), showing its ability to handle seasonal data patterns. Real-time energy data (kWh) from the hospital, collected every 30 minutes over 6 months, was analyzed. The best model identified was SARIMA (2,0,0) x (1,1,1)24 for forecasting missing weekday data with seasonal patterns. The model’s parameters were evaluated, achieving an MSE of 2144.94514 and an RMSE of 46.31355. The model’s accuracy was further evaluated by comparing the actual and forecasted values, taking into account the complex correlation of socioeconomic factors affecting energy usage.

articleTitle: Design of WDM Fiber-FSO System Using EDFA and FBG for An Interbuilding Communication Link
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The demand for a better and more capable telecommunication system continues to increase as other technologies advance. Telecommunication systems are facing a major problem in order to achieve higher capacity. To address this problem, a more capable system with higher capacity, yet reliable is required. This research offers a solution to this problem by improving the Fiber-FSO system using WDM technology. The key is to achieve larger capacities using multiple canals in the WDM method. This research proposes the usage of the 4 canal WDM component (193.1–193.4 THz) for the Fiber-FSO system. The design of the WDM Fiber-FSO system using EDFA and FBG proposed in this research reaches up to 80 Gb/s of data rate. This result is significantly higher when compared to other regular Fiber-FSO systems. One of many implementations of this system is the interbuilding communication system. For this implementation, a long-range system is necessary. This research provides an interbuilding communication system with fiber optic range extending up to 10 km per side and FSO media range reaching up to 10 km. The performance of the system will be measured mainly using the Q factor and minimum BER. At normal attenuation of 1 dB/km, the proposed design system reaches the best result averagely when given 10 dBm of power input. The average performance result in this scenario reaches Q Factor 6.78 on average. This performance result is in accordance with the standard given for the proposed design with the Q factor that requires the value of 6. The proposed design will be tested in several weather conditions in metropolitan cities, with attenuation in the FSO media reaching 20 dB/km for the worst conditions. The result of the design test under several conditions shows that the system will need to sacrifice the FSO media range as conditions worsen to achieve acceptable results.

articleTitle: Surveillance Video Analytics for Automated Detection of Personal Protective Equipment using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: As Malaysia continues its rapid development, ensuring worker safety at construction sites has become a paramount concern. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) plays a critical role in preventing accidents, but manual monitoring of PPE compliance is often inefficient and prone to errors. This paper presents a video analytics system designed to detect PPE violations and automate people counting using state-of-the-art deep learning models, YOLO-NAS and YOLOv8. The system focuses on identifying PPE compliance by detecting helmets and safety vests with at least 50% overlap within the bounding box of detected individuals. Compliance violations are flagged, enabling real-time interventions. The system was tested on a variety of video samples captured from construction sites, achieving accuracy rates between 50% and 76% in detecting PPE violations and counting individuals. The varying accuracy values stem from challenges such as video quality and recording angles. Although there are these shortcomings, the proposed system is still capable of significantly improving the PPE monitoring process, reducing manual supervision errors, and enhancing overall workplace safety.

articleTitle: Loan Eligibility Prediction Using Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques and SMOTE
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Loans play important roles in banking sectors. Loans provide bank income and fuel growth for the banking industry itself. Loans that are provided to the lender should be repaid on schedule to the bank. Therefore, banks need to carefully evaluate each customer whether they will repay the loan back. However, some institutions find difficulties to accurately predicting whether the customers are good defaulters or bad defaulters. With the existence of machine learning technologies, many financial institutions seek cutting-edge technologies. To simplify the process of approving customers’ eligibility for the loan banking system. In this paper, we will use Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), and LightGBM (LGBM) to improve loan eligibility predictions. With this model we are using several data preprocessing methods such as handling missing values, Handling outliers, one-hot encoding, and oversampling (SMOTE). Overall evaluation metrics will be measured with Accuracy, Recall, Precision, and F1 scores to determine which model provides the highest Score. In this paper, our XGBoost model gives the best output measured with more than 95% in every evaluation metric.

articleTitle: uitPDFXAI: Malicious PDF files detection with eXplainable Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: There are many security incidents related to PDF (Portable Document Format) files. Many studies have been proposed to detect malicious PDF files. In this study, we propose uitPDFXAI system to detect malicious PDF files by leveraging the powerful machine learning algorithms XGBoost and AdaBoost. Utilizing the SHapley Additive exPlanations, an explainable Artificial Intelligence, we provide a detailed explanation of the contribution of features to the model’s predictions, enhancing the transparency and interpretability. Our experiments are conducted on the CIC-Evasive-PDFMal2022 dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed system achieves the highest accuracy of 99.55% when using XGBoost. When using AdaBoost the system’s accuracy is 98.90%. The results of this study can be used for future research in the field of malicious PDF file detection.

articleTitle: Bi-LSTM Approach for Seagrass Transplantation Site Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Seagrasses form crucial ecosystems globally, supporting diverse communities and providing essential ecological and socioeconomic benefits. However, these ecosystems are under threat, necessitating effective restoration strategies. This study proposed Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) approach to identify and evaluate optimal sites for seagrass transplantation. The dataset comprising files containing key environmental parameters such as temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, pH, total suspended solids, and bathymetry, was used to train and validate the Bi-LSTM model. The model achieved initial training and validation accuracy are 98.75% and 99.98% respectively, also training and validation loss are 0.0326 and 0.0112 respectively within 10 epochs. A comparative analysis with Echo State Networks (ESN) and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN-1D) demonstrated that the Bi-LSTM model significantly outperformed these alternatives, achieving superior prediction accuracy. The model was further validated using environmental data from Dompak Island in Indonesia, with the predictions visualized through QGIS. The Bi-LSTM model exhibited high performance, with an average accuracy of 88.38% and the mean squared error (MSE) of 11.615%. Furthermore, the model’s potential in supporting the strategic restoration and preservation of coastal ecosystems was highlighted. This study provides environmental professionals with a powerful analytical tool for enhancing seagrass cover, water quality, marine habitats, and carbon sequestration processes. Future research could focus on developing a real-time predictive tool integrated with various sensors to further improve the efficiency and accuracy of seagrass transplantation site detection. This would ensure continuous up-dates and immediate feedback based on real-time environmental data.

articleTitle: Design And Development Of A Rain Gauge System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Measuring rainfall is an essential part of gathering meteorological data. However, the precision and real-time monitoring capabilities of traditional rain gauges are frequently limited. This study describes the design and development of a rain gauge device that uses innovative parts and technology to monitor precipitation with increased accuracy and efficiency. The device’s ability to accurately detect rainfall and measure its volume is made possible by the integration of Hall effect sensors and rainwater sensors, which guarantees that its primary function is effectively carried out. Utilizing the ESP32 Development Board improves the rain gauge device’s performance and dependability by facilitating smooth data collecting. Furthermore, the utilization of LoRa modules in data transmission facilitates the reliable and long-range transfer of rainfall data, guaranteeing its accessibility and usage in diverse contexts. In addition, the implementation of a LoRaWAN cloud server allowed for the centralized reception of data from various rain gauge devices, facilitating the real-time monitoring and analysis of rainfall trends. These developments helped to offer a reliable and comprehensive system for accurate and effective rainfall measurement.

articleTitle: YOLOv5-GT: A Balanced Improvement in Object Detection Speed and Accuracy for Autonomous Vehicles in Indonesian Mixed Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Object detection speed and accuracy are critical aspects of the perception system in autonomous vehicles. Speed improvement helps the object detector model achieve performance close to real-time, while accuracy enhancement ensures robust detection across various scenes. Balancing these improvements enhances the safety of autonomous vehicles, particularly in mixed and dense traffic conditions, such as those in Indonesia. This study develops a detection model using local datasets to reflect real-world conditions. It achieved balanced improvements in frames per second (fps) and mean Average Precision (mAP@50–95) through a modified YOLOv5 deep learning model. The key enhancements of the model include the integration of GhostConv and Transformer layers into the YOLOv5 architecture, referred to as YOLOv5s-GT, as well as the application of image augmentations with various scenarios to the training data. Experimental results show that the modified YOLOv5 outperformed the baseline model in both fps and mAP metrics, achieving 82.6 fps and 80.1% mAP@50–95, compared to the baseline performance of 75.8 fps and 77.7% mAP@50–95.

articleTitle: Improving Furnace Coil Outlet Temperature Measurement: Comparative Performance of Dual-Wavelength Pyrometer and Type-K Thermocouple
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: In the rigorous environments of industrial furnaces, accurate measurement of Furnace Coil Outlet Temperature (COT) is crucial for maintaining efficiency, safety, and product quality. Traditional thermocouple, while commonly used, suffer from degradation and drift due to harsh conditions, leading to inaccurate measurements and frequent maintenance needs. This paper presents a comparative study of the performance of advanced dual-wavelength pyrometer versus traditional Type-K thermocouple in measuring COT. It explores the response time, accuracy, stability against thermal cycles, and maintainability of these measurement technologies. The study reveals that dual-wavelength pyrometer not only provide faster response times in conditions of rapid temperature changes, but also offer superior accuracy and stability under thermal cycling, reducing the need for frequent recalibration. The pyrometer exhibited response times approximately 2 minutes faster than the thermocouple in reaching temperature stabilization. Over extended periods, the thermocouple showed deviations up to 18°C of average difference, especially after thermal cycling events. Despite its higher cost and the increased complexity in setup, due to the need for external power supplies and precise alignment, the pyrometer demonstrates significant benefits in high-temperature industrial settings. These findings are pivotal for industries where precise temperature control is essential, recommending a shift toward non-contact pyrometry for reliable, long-term temperature monitoring in challenging furnace operations.

articleTitle: Revealing Malaysian NFT Art: Exploring Opportunities and Price Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) have made a significant impact on the Malaysian art industry. This blockchain advancement have provided artists with a new way to monetize their digital artworks and have also opened avenues for art enthusiasts to collect and trade digital art in a secure and transparent manner. Many Malaysian artists have embraced NFTs as a means of showcasing and selling their digital creations to a global audience. However, the pricing factors of NFTs have posed obstacles for traditional artists and collectors who wish to enter this technology. This research paper aims to study the elements that influence the pricing of NFTs created by Malaysian artists. The study conducted interviews with prominent Malaysian NFT creator that has successfully created and monetized their NFTs on both local and international platforms which was analyzed using thematic analysis. This analysis reveals that market dynamics, creator reputation, and the concept of scarcity and utility influence the pricing factors of NFTs in Malaysia. These insights provide a comprehensive understanding of the multifaceted factors that shape the NFT pricing in Malaysia. The findings underscore the necessity for educational initiatives to enhance understanding of NFT market among artists and collectors. This study also proposes for future research to explore the long-term evolution of the NFT market and to compare it with other regional and global markets to gain comprehensive insights into its dynamics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Social Media Accessibility: Automatic Alternative Text Generation in X by Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: In the contemporary digital landscape, social media’s reliance on visual content poses significant accessibility barriers for individuals with visual impairments, sidelining a substantial user base. This study applies Artificial Intelligence to improve accessibility on social media by automating alternative text generation for images on platform X (formerly Twitter). The Generative Image-to-text Transformer (GIT) model is analyzed and then integrated with the Twitter API. Using the Flickr30k dataset, further fine-tuning and evaluation processes are performed on the model. Concurrently, the model demonstrates higher accuracy of 106% over the baseline VGG model as quantified by ROUGE metrics. The results confirm our model’s capability to produce descriptive and contextually relevant captions that significantly enhance accessibility for visually impaired users. Furthermore, the integration of this AI-driven solution into social media platforms showcases the practical application of advanced machine learning techniques in addressing real-world accessibility challenges. This research highlights the potential of AI to transform digital communication, making it more inclusive and ensuring that visually impaired users can fully participate in the social media experience.

articleTitle: Comparing Hate Speech Detection Machine Learning Models Trained on Authentic and Translated Indonesian Data
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Social media is growing exponentially, it has become a place where people can express themself freely. However, not often that hate speech can be found in the expressions. It is important to prevent hate speech as it is harmful for our society. There has been a lot of research about the detection of hate speech using artificial intelligence however most of this research focuses on the models, there is a few research that focuses on the data rather than the model. Our research aims to find the effects of the data itself towards the performance of the models. We achieve this by having two separate datasets: hate speech in Indonesian and hate speech in English which is translated into Indonesian using Google translate Service. We use these datasets separately into several machine learning models including Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF). The best result was achieved by the RF model with 75% accuracy and weighted average F1 score for the Indonesian dataset and 58% accuracy and weighted average F1 score for the translated dataset. The Indonesian dataset is proven to be superior than the translated dataset.

articleTitle: Trends in Technological Areas using Patent Analytics: A Comparative Study on the Time Series Forecasting of International Patent Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Intellectual Properties like Patents, Utility Models, Industrial Designs, and Copyrights are considered the drivers of today’s modern knowledge-based economy. The number of registered and granted Intellectual Properties is one key performance indicator of a state in advancing science and technology. Thus, analyzing the trends is vital as it sets directions for the state. This study aims to analyze the patent trends in the International Patent Classification by incorporating various classical statistical-based techniques and algorithms in time series forecasting. This leads to the generation of insight into the present and future of registered and granted intellectual properties. Autoregression, Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving-Average and Holt Winter’s Exponential Smoothing are the classical time series forecasting algorithms that were compared using three performance indicators, i.e., Root Mean Square Errors, Mean Absolute Errors, and the Coefficient of Determination. It was concluded that the seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average achieved a high performance of several indicators per section. However, it is vital to consider the behaviour of the present data and the appropriate time series forecasting algorithms for forecasting, thus having it on a case-to-case basis.

articleTitle: Efficient IoT-Based Processing For Coastal Erosion Vulnerability Assessment Using Multispectral Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Coastal erosion is a severe threat to the environment impacting many coastal areas throughout the world. The increasing rate and severity of erosion occurrences can be due to a combination of natural and human sources. Coastal erosion is becoming more prevalent through rising sea levels, climate change, and human activities including urbanisation and unsustainable coastal development. The study aims to examine the geographical and chronological patterns of coastal erosion along the shoreline of Kuala Rompin, Pahang for a long-term period, specifically from 2003 to 2023. Over the past twenty-years, coastline features and coastal erosion rate were revealed by utilizing Landsat and Satellite optical imagery. Additionally, with the desired satellite revisit timeframe, the combination of high-resolution multi spectral data and advanced GIS spatial analysis tools comprehensive change detection to assess the dynamic pattern and vulnerability rate of coastal landscape. Analysis of the data indicates an average erosion rate of −9.52 meters per year, with significant variability along the coastline. Besides that, this study also delved deeper into the relationship between environmental factors and the likelihood of erosion, offering useful insights into the factors that caused changes in the coastal area. The utilization of GIS and Remote Sensing images in this study provided a flexible and adaptable framework in the form of classified remote sensing images and GIS models complete with analysis for evaluating the susceptibility of coastal areas in different regions, promoting a wider range of potential applications for the research findings to aid other departments in mitigating and preventing coastal erosion in the area. The findings provide an enhance comprehension of the dynamics of coastal erosion around Kuala Rompin, facilitating well-informed decision-making for the implementation of sustainable methods in coastal management. In summary, this research can serve as a significant reference for environmental scientists, policymakers, and coastal management practitioners involved in addressing the effects of erosion on susceptible coastal regions.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Multi-Task Learning Using StridedConv3D-VideoSwin for Video Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) is the problem of identifying anomalous events in the temporal space from the given video data. The studies in VAD domain are still challenging because the definitions of anomalies are quite varied, the data limitations to describe anomalous events, and the anomalous data tends to be relatively close to normal data. The limitations of labeled data have made several studies focus learning only on dominant data, normal events, which is often known as the One-Class Classification (OCC). Self-Supervised Multi-Task Learning (SSMTL), one of the architectures in OCC, still uses a pure CNN-based encoder, which does not maximize the global information usage in feature extraction from each data input. Meanwhile, in the OCC development, many studies have utilized transformers which have better effectiveness, especially in adversarial attacks. On the other side, CNN has advantages regarding considering inductive bias in learning local spatial context. Therefore, this study aims to use Video Shift-Window Transformer (VideoSwin) architecture for video data feature extraction by implementing 3D Convolutional Neural Net (Conv3D) in video patch embedding, StridedConv3D-VideoSwin. The application of StridedConv3d-VideoSwin in SSMTL provides performance improvement for predicting anomaly scores on the pedestrian activity domain. These results consider the detection with Macro and Micro AUC metrics on the CUHK Avenue, UCSD Ped2, and ShanghaiTech datasets. Furthermore, it provides less memory usage even though the floating point operations increases by 74.42%.

articleTitle: The Evolution of Dynamic Line Rating: Technological Advancements and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Dynamic Line Rating (DLR) is a cutting-edge technology implemented in the power transmission industry to enhance the efficiency and reliability of electricity networks. Unlike traditional static line ratings, which rely on conservative estimates of worst-case environmental conditions, DLR utilizes real-time data on vicinity, weather, and line status to dynamically adjust the permissible load on transmission lines. DLR methodologies provide a more accurate assessment of thermal capacity, maximize the use of existing infrastructure, and facilitate the integration of renewable energy sources. Despite its advantages, DLR implementation faces challenges, including the need for sophisticated monitoring equipment, robust data processing capabilities, and modified thermal models. This paper aims to chronicle the evolution of DLR, discuss major technological advancements, and explore future directions in the field of overhead lines and underground transmission cables. The review covers the historical context of DLR, current technological trends, emerging methodologies, DLR studies in tropical and subtropical regions, and the impact of DLR. By examining these themes, the paper provides a comprehensive overview of DLR technology, highlighting future research areas where DLR could transform power system operations and support the transition to a more flexible, efficient, and sustainable energy grid.

articleTitle: Automatic landmark detection in cephalometric lateral radiograph using deep learning one-stage detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Cephalometric radiography is the gold standard in analyzing, assessing, and diagnosing the relationship between teeth, jaws, and skeletal structures. In previous studies, artificial intelligence has been widely used to identify anatomical landmarks on lateral cephalometric radiographs, reducing errors and speeding up the analysis. This research aims to explore the automation of the landmarks detection process using You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5). A total of 350 cephalometric radiographs were selected as learning data that trained YOLOv5 and the number of target labels was 17 pairs of landmark. The assessment is evaluated by mean radial error, success detection rate, and matrix evaluation. The system’s accuracy in predicting 17 pairs of landmarks in the image within the error range of 2 mm reaches 90.44% on average and the MRE result is 0.9553 mm. The matrix evaluation results show the confidence value show that the most successful predictions were obtained from Sella (1.00), Menton (0.94), Intermolar (0.93), and the worst from LA (0.04), point B (0.47), and UA (0.14). The YOLOv5 model demonstrates strong landmark detection capabilities but still needs improvement. To achieve the same level of robustness as the gold standard, further research can focus on enhancing datasets and improving YOLO models.

articleTitle: Protocols Performance Evaluation : Smartphone’s Battery and Mobile Data Usage Based on LBS Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Location-Based Services (LBS) are a crucial component of on-demand cellular telephones, requiring precise location as part of the service process. These services utilize the Global Positioning Service (GPS) on cellphones to determine location. In LBS applications that need near real-time or real-time location availability, geolocation data is periodically sent and then transmitted back to the recipient’s mobile device, completing one service cycle. A significant challenge is the high consumption of power and cellular data on these devices. Selecting the appropriate protocol optimizes the reduction of power and cellular data usage in mobile devices when utilizing LBS applications. The protocols tested included HTTP, WebSocket, AMQP, and gRPC, with client and server applications specifically designed for this testing. The HTTP protocol has been proven effective for sending geolocation data in LBS application development, with a primary focus on battery efficiency and independence from cellular data usage volume. The gRPC protocol is more suitable when minimizing cellular data usage is a priority, considering battery power consumption, and it is the optimal choice for receiving geolocation data. For applications requiring minimal battery power usage to receive geolocation data, the WebSocket protocol is the ideal choice.

articleTitle: Applicability of Indian Construction Risk Factors in the Philippines: Assessment of Time, Cost, and Quality Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: As a developing country, the Philippines is one of the expanding countries in the construction industry. Analyzing risks in construction building projects and developing a precise method to predict them have always been challenging for project managers. The traditional method has been used for decades however, it has been proven that using the Design-Build (DB) method shows improved outcomes in cost and schedule. Nonetheless, some risks need to be considered. Having similarities and differences with India as regards construction sectors, geography, and development level, this study aimed to identify how significant the adopted risk factors are in the DB construction within the Philippines and created a model to predict the mean impact of risk factors under Time, Cost, and Quality (TCQ) in DB building projects using Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). Employing advanced techniques such as spearman’s correlation, relative importance index method, ANN pearson, and fishbone analysis to compare risk factors adopted from India to the Philippines. The findings of this study will help the engineers, designers, contractors, and owners determine the relevance of risk factors in terms of TCQ that can be applied to their projects.

articleTitle: Crafting Effective Prompts: A Guideline for Successful Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: AI’s ability to convert text into high-quality visuals is revolutionizing a number of study sectors, including the creative industries. This work focuses on how prompt construction plays a crucial role in maximizing large language models’ (LLMs’) efficacy in image production. While prompt engineering encompasses many study fields, this work focuses primarily on how prompts should be designed to enhance the quality of generated images utilizing prompt anatomy as input. In this study, two student groups were compared: one group produced photos on their own without any supervision, and the other group was given tips on how to make efficient suggestions. Clarity, detail, relevance, aesthetic appeal, and inventiveness were the criteria used to assess the prompts and the final photos. According to the panel of experts evaluating the results, the group who received guided prompt creation generated photos that were both much better and more in line with the intended concept. This work emphasizes how crucial good prompt design is for AI-driven image production and shows that appropriate prompt crafting training can significantly improve output quality. These results offer a foundation for the more efficient application of AI technologies and have important ramifications for AI-assisted design, education, and the creative industries.

articleTitle: Dog Emotion Classification using Vision Transformer Models
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Dog expressions encapsulate crucial information that reflects their current emotional states, providing an innovative approach to interpret their feelings. Although many papers have explored facial expression recognition (FER) in humans using artificial intelligence, similar research done on dogs is lacking. In this paper, we experiment to predict the emotional state of dogs broken down into 4 categories: angry, happy, relaxed, and sad. We use Mask-RCNN to handle preprocessing and utilize state of the art vision transformer (ViT) models such as dinov2-base-imagenetlk-1-layer and beit-base-patch16-224-pt22k-ft22k to analyze and classify canine emotions. Among the models, both vision transformer models achieved the overall highest accuracies compared to the CNN models. The results state that DINOv2 has the highest accuracy, followed by BeiT with the overall accuracy 84.68% and 84.50%, respectively. Color Jitter preprocessing boosts the accuracy approximately 1.98% higher than Gray Scaling. However, upon further analysis of individual class breakdowns, it was observed that BeiT models outperformed DINOv2 in the happy category, while ResNet surpassed DINOv2 in the relaxed category.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Energy Forecasting Accuracy Using LSTM Networks for Global Horizontal Irradiance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This paper introduces an approach for enhancing solar energy predictions through Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, utilizing Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) data. The generation of solar energy is increasingly vital in tackling the global energy crisis and facilitating the shift to renewable energy sources. Thus, accurate forecasting of solar irradiance trends, especially GHI, is essential for optimizing the efficiency and dependability of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Current techniques often struggle to account for the intricate temporal relationships in GHI data, resulting in less accurate forecasts. Our study aims to address these shortcomings by leveraging LSTM networks, which are specifically crafted to model long-term dependencies in time-series data. We explored two models: one relying solely on historical GHI data and another that incorporates additional weather factors such as Global Tilt Irradiance (GTI), temperature, Diffuse Horizontal Irradiance (DHI), and Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI), all of which have shown strong correlations with GHI trends. Both models were trained and assessed using a dataset from Solcast, focusing on the Shah Alam area in Malaysia. In addition, simulations of photovoltaic (PV) energy generation were conducted based on GHI predictions to illustrate the practical use of these forecasts in real-world applications. The proposed models were evaluated with performance metrics including Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The results indicate that incorporating additional meteorological parameters enhances prediction accuracy, with the second model demonstrating lower training and validation losses. These findings imply that LSTM models, like the one proposed, hold significant promise for improving the accuracy and reliability of solar energy forecasts, serving as a valuable asset for renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: A Study on the Navigation and Control Methods for Turtlebot3 Robot Using ROS
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This paper reports a study on the design of a control methodology for a differential drive wheeled mobile robot (DDWMR) that integrates smooth reference trajectory generation using Bézier curves with a proportional (P) controller to achieve the aforementioned tasks. The proposed methodology first generates a polynomial function-type reference trajectory to seamlessly connect the initial and final poses of the DDWMR. Subsequently, a P control law is designed to enable the DDWMR to track the pre-generated reference trajectory with minimum transient and steady-stat errors. By integrating Bézier curve-based trajectory planning with a P control approach, the proposed approach offers an efficient solution for autonomous navigation of DDWMRs and also addresses the complexities posed by their nonholonomic constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is shown through simulations on MATLAB and robot operating system (ROS) softwares which demonstrate the robot’s ability to perform collision-free movement and navigation.

articleTitle: A Web-based Management System for Diagnostic Laboratory with Business Process Re-Engineering and Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Management information systems are a challenge for many small businesses. With fast-changing technology, data management has become an integral part of business processes, especially in the healthcare industry. This study uses Business Process Re-Engineering (BPR) and Data Analytics for a Diagnostic Laboratory to improve its operational efficiency through a web-based management system. The obsolete system, consisting of eight modules, is replaced with a sophisticated system involving twenty-one modules. The goal is to evaluate the impact of technology on business operations and user satisfaction. The results indicate that the most recent technology enables board members to monitor corporate performance from any location using various web browsers. The database securely saves and categorizes all operational data. Transactions, test results, and reports are instantly created in PDF format. Subsequently, the gathered information is utilized by means of descriptive and prescriptive analysis. The system acceptance is also assessed using a questionnaire that adheres to the ISO 25010 standards. With an optimal score of 5.0, the results showed a weighted average of 4.79 (“Strongly Agree”), which is significantly higher than the prior system average of 3.69 (“Agree”). The conclusions emphasize that the system has a crucial role in remote management, efficient database management, improved operational efficiency, and reduced turnaround time. Recommendations encompass the integration of digital payment methods for transactions and advocating the established system as a benchmark for other diagnostic laboratories in the health industry. This research has a significant impact on the improvement of diagnostic laboratory management systems.
